Notes

A threatening, self-admiring persona guards the right to look at itself, while appetite and insecurity remain visible under the red-carpet confidence.

请你先想清楚

请 supplies “please” to a warning surrounded by threats, so courtesy is doing coercive work. The later promise to stop being polite makes that tension explicit. The speaker presents himself as someone whose boundaries are reasonable and whose retaliation will be the other person’s responsibility. The civil phrasing is part of the threatening posture.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
利刃出鞘

利刃出鞘 is a compact, dramatic image of a weapon being drawn. Its four-character form and the impossible speed that follows give the threat a staged, cinematic sharpness. The target is specifically the eyes, preparing a song preoccupied with looking and reflection. The next admission of being deep in a role keeps that performance frame in view.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
没有骨气

骨气, literally “bone spirit,” means backbone or integrity: the ability to stand one’s ground. “Spineless” preserves a comparable bodily image. The insult follows the spectacular threat to another person’s eyes, making moral weakness physically legible. It is the vocabulary of a speaker measuring worth through firmness, even while insisting that others must stop judging him.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
选择权在我

选择权 does not just mean a preference; it is the right or power to choose. The sentence makes sovereignty over the self the core claim beneath the insults. Yet the planned red carpet and arriving reporters show that this self still anticipates an audience. The song seeks control over the terms of attention rather than total disappearance.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
腥味

腥味 is the raw, fishy or bloody smell of flesh. 人多 makes it increase with the number of people, so a crowd becomes a bodily substance before it becomes company. Generic “stench” conveys disgust but loses that fleshy specificity. The line supplies a sensory rationale for withdrawal within this particularly hostile persona.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
入戏太深

入戏太深 means becoming too absorbed in a dramatic role. The next line insists he is never confused, so the speaker separates immersion from losing awareness. That distinction matters for the violence, mirror-admiration and red carpet that follow: he can perform the role intensely while also describing it as a role. The contradiction is visible within the lyric itself.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
独善其身

独善其身 can praise maintaining one’s own integrity, but it can also criticize looking after only oneself. Both meanings are documented in the dictionary. “Selfish and conceited” soon follows, preventing a purely virtuous reading. The compact phrase lets self-preservation and self-absorption touch: keeping oneself intact may also mean withdrawing concern from everybody else.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 獨善其身
目不转睛

目不转睛 means fixing the gaze without turning the eyes away. Earlier the speaker imagined destroying another person’s eyes; here he cannot stop looking at his own reflection. The repeated eye imagery organizes the song’s power: outside looking is treated as intrusion, while his own looking supplies approval. “Flawless” arrives as a verdict from the gaze he permits.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
完美无瑕

无瑕 means without a blemish. The mirror produces complete satisfaction here, but “Sweet” later turns a demon-revealing mirror on the self to expose its true nature. Those two uses offer a useful contrast: reflection can flatter or uncover. The album does not give every mirror scene the same reassuring function.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
红地毯已铺好

The scene moves from the private mirror to a prepared public entrance: carpet ready, reporters on the way. It makes the self-admiration part of a performance that is about to be seen. Hurry replaces contemplation. Even within the fantasy of complete control, somebody else’s arrival sets the timetable.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
不能再当一个好人

不能再 frames goodness as a role that can no longer be sustained, and the next line supplies the reason: privately counted traps. The claim is more revealing than a simple boast of cruelty. It casts the hardened persona as something learned from injury, while the lyric still lets us hear how convenient that explanation can be for the speaker.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
胃口

胃口 means appetite and can extend to the scale of somebody’s demands. Saying it is small makes the request sound modest, but the next line still fears not having enough. That insecurity survives all the flawless reflection and red-carpet expectation. The body wants a guarantee the public image cannot provide.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
得了癌症却不敢治疗

The closing accusation pictures an extreme condition being left untreated while spending continues. It ends the contrast between the speaker’s fear of hunger and other people’s waste with an image of denial. The sharp turn from money to the body makes the accusation more than ordinary envy: resources are plentiful, but facing damage is continually deferred.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
